what_its_for: Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections such as skin infections, lung infections, pelvic infections, dental infections, and bone infections. It works by stopping the growth of bacteria. It is NOT used for viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take clindamycin capsules by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces) to prevent irritation of your throat and food pipe. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Swallow capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure the dose carefully with the measuring spoon or syringe provided. Take every dose at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep a steady amount of medicine in your body. Finish ALL of your medication even if you start to feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your infection type, age, and weight. Common adult doses range from 150 mg to 450 mg taken every 6 to 8 hours. For children, the dose is based on body weight and is determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store capsules and tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C), away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep liquid clindamycin at room temperature — do NOT refrigerate or freeze it, as it may thicken and become hard to use. Liquid clindamycin is good for 2 weeks at room temperature, so discard any unused portion after that time. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking clindamycin with antidiarrheal medications (like loperamide/Imodium) if you develop diarrhea, as this can make certain serious infections worse — call your doctor first. Avoid alcohol, as it may worsen stomach upset. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially erythromycin (these two antibiotics can work against each other). Avoid taking any new medications, vitamins, or supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe or watery diarrhea (with or without blood or mucus) that does not go away — this could be a serious bowel infection called C. difficile; severe stomach cramps or pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe skin reactions such as blistering, peeling, or red skin; or signs of a new infection. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment or if they get worse.
when_it_works: Most people begin to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting clindamycin. However, it is very important to keep taking all of your medication even if you feel better, because stopping early can allow the bacteria to come back and become harder to treat. The full course of treatment is usually 7 to 14 days, depending on the type of infection.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Clindamycin can pass into breast milk and may affect a nursing baby. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before prescribing it. Children: Clindamycin can be used in children, but the dose is carefully calculated based on body weight by the doctor. Do not give this medication to newborns without specific doctor guidance. Older Adults: Older adults may be at higher risk for certain side effects, especially severe diarrhea. Liver or Kidney Disease: If you have liver or kidney problems, tell your doctor before taking this medication, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Allergies: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to clindamycin or lincomycin before taking this medicine.
